examples.question_text: A car has a tare weight of $1420\text{ kg}$ and is registered for business use. Using the supplied historical vehicle-tax table in the teaching, determine the vehicle tax payable.
examples.solution_text:
The tare weight is in the $1155\text{ to }1504\text{ kg}$ row. Read across to the business use column.

$\text{Vehicle tax}=\$564$

examples.question_text: A vehicle has a purchase price and market value of $\$31\,800$. Using the supplied booklet's historical stamp-duty method, calculate the stamp duty payable.
examples.solution_text:
The value is below $\$45\,000$, so apply $3\%$ to the whole value.

$\begin{align*}\text{Stamp duty}&=0.03\times\$31\,800\\&=\$954\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A vehicle has a purchase price and market value of $\$61\,200$. Using the supplied booklet's historical stamp-duty method, calculate the stamp duty payable.
examples.solution_text:
Calculate the excess above $\$45\,000$.

$\begin{align*}\text{Excess}&=\$61\,200-\$45\,000\\&=\$16\,200\end{align*}$

Apply $3\%$ to the first $\$45\,000$ and $5\%$ to the excess.

$\begin{align*}\text{Stamp duty}&=0.03\times\$45\,000+0.05\times\$16\,200\\&=\$1350+\$810\\&=\$2160\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A driver is quoted $\$1120$ for comprehensive car insurance and has a $35\%$ no-claim bonus. Calculate the premium payable.
examples.solution_text:
A $35\%$ no-claim bonus is a discount, so the driver pays $100\%-35\%=65\%$ of the quoted premium.

$\begin{align*}\text{Premium payable}&=0.65\times\$1120\\&=\$728\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: 1420 kg lies within 1155–1504 kg. The supplied table gives $564 for business use.
31800 is below the 45000 threshold. Stamp duty = 0.03 × 31800 = $954.
Excess = 61200 − 45000 = 16200. Duty on the first 45000 = 1350; duty on the excess = 0.05 × 16200 = 810. Total stamp duty = $2160.
